title: BotConfigArtifact
description: Published, cross-boundary bot-config contract an external engine consumes to boot a bot. Field names are the external API; evolve via schema_version. The language-neutral source of truth for the BotConfigArtifact dataclass.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Distinct from the per-bot content 'version'.

version.description: Per-bot content version. Always present; an integer for a published service-bot snapshot, null for a live personal/draft bot.

engine_overrides.description: Bot-specific overrides (e.g. channels) the engine applies to its own base config. The engine base config (teclaw.json / openclaw.json) is engine-owned and NOT produced here.

identity_files.description: User/platform-authored workspace files (e.g. RULES.md). Engine-generated files are referenced via engine_ext, not here.

cli_tools.description: Command-line tools the model can invoke (schema_version 5+). Deliberately NOT in 'required': an absent key means 'not declared - leave the bot's tools alone', an explicit [] means 'remove every manifest-delivered tool'. Those are different instructions.

stores.description: Physical coordinates of content stores, keyed by store_id (the source scheme; name it for the store, not the scope). Location only — NEVER credentials. A ref {store:'skill-repo', path:'team/x'} resolves against stores['skill-repo'].

engine_ext.description: Opaque, engine-owned free-form JSON (pointers/metadata, e.g. MEMORY.md/IDENTITY.md references). The backend stores/freezes/returns it verbatim and never interprets it.

storeRef.description: Content store coordinates (location only, never credentials).

base.description: Key prefix within the bucket / root path.

endpoint.description: Optional access endpoint; engine config supplies it if absent.

fileRef.description: A file reference: 'store' keys into 'stores' for the physical location; 'path' is relative within that store.

path.description: Path relative to the store (e.g. 'team/weather'); placement decided by the engine owner.

cliToolRef.description: One command-line tool: one entry = one command = one file. The platform fetches, enforces the declared sha256, unpacks an archive form and selects the one declared file, so 'path' always names a single executable file - never a directory, and never something the engine has to pick from a tree.

name.description: Tool identifier AND the command name the agent invokes (e.g. 'mycli', not an absolute path). Unique per bot and free of path separators, both enforced at write time.

path.description: Path relative to the store, naming the single executable file; physical placement and PATH exposure decided by the engine owner.

md5.description: Platform-computed MD5 (32 lowercase hex) of the bytes at 'path', for the engine to verify what it retrieves. NOT the store's ETag - a multipart upload's ETag is not the content MD5.

version.description: Optional audit/display metadata; the engine need not interpret it.

mcpServerRef.description: One MCP server, in one of two mutually exclusive forms discriminated by 'transport'. The 'oneOf' below is the authority: a local entry ('stdio') must carry a launch instruction — top-level 'command'/'args'/'env' — and no endpoint/headers; a remote entry ('http'/'sse') must carry no launch instruction. Validating against this schema is enough to reject a half-formed entry — no engine-side launch attempt required.

endpoint.description: Remote form. May carry an inlined ?authorization=<token> query.

headers.description: Remote form. May carry inlined secret headers (e.g. x-ling-auth).

command.description: Local form (transport == 'stdio'): the executable the engine spawns as a child process, speaking JSON-RPC over its stdin/stdout, e.g. 'python3'. Carries no credentials — the child runs inside the engine's own container. Null/absent for a remote server.

args.description: Local form. Arguments for 'command'. Empty/absent for a remote server.

env.description: Local form. Environment variables for the child process. Empty/absent for a remote server.

oneOf.title: local (stdio)
oneOf.description: transport 'stdio' ⇒ a launch instruction, and none of the remote fields.

oneOf.title: remote (http/sse)
oneOf.description: transport 'http'/'sse' ⇒ a URL to connect to, and no launch instruction. 'endpoint' is required here even though it is nullable at the top level: an entry with neither a URL nor a launch instruction gives the engine nothing to act on.
